title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Abstract class** | A class that cannot be instantiated; it shares code and declares abstract methods subclasses must implement. (3.04) |
| **Access modifier** | `public`, `protected`, `private` or none (package-private): who may use a member. (3.02) |
| **Amortised O(1)** | Usually constant time, with rare expensive steps that average out, like `ArrayList.add`. (5.04) |
| **Annotation** | A label on code written with `@`, read by the compiler, frameworks or reflection. (7.03) |
| **Anonymous class** | A class declared and created in one expression, with no name. (7.01) |
| **Array** | A fixed-size, indexed sequence of values of one type. (2.02) |
| **ArrayList** | A list backed by an array that grows as needed. (2.03) |
| **Autoboxing** | Automatic conversion between a primitive and its wrapper, such as `int` and `Integer`. (2.03) |
| **Base case** | The input a recursive method answers directly, without calling itself. (2.04) |
| **Big O** | Notation for how an algorithm's work grows with input size, ignoring constants. (5.01) |
| **Binary search** | Finding a value in a sorted array by halving the range each step: O(log n). (5.02) |
| **Binary search tree** | A binary tree where left subtrees hold smaller keys and right subtrees larger ones. (5.05) |
| **Builder pattern** | A helper object that collects settings step by step and then creates an immutable object. (7.01) |
| **ByteBuffer** | A buffer of bytes with a chosen byte order and methods to read and write numbers. (7.05) |
| **Bytecode** | The instructions `javac` produces for the Java Virtual Machine. (1.01) |
| **Cast** | An explicit conversion, such as `(int) 3.9`. (1.02) |
| **Checked exception** | An exception that must be caught or declared with `throws`, such as `IOException`. (4.04) |
| **Class** | A blueprint for objects: fields, constructors and methods. (3.01) |
| **Clock** | A source of the current time that can be fixed in tests. (7.04) |
| **Collection** | The interface of groups of objects: lists, sets and queues. (4.02) |
| **Comparable** | The interface giving a class its natural order through `compareTo`. (3.04) |
| **Comparator** | An ordering kept outside the compared class. (4.03) |
| **Consistent with equals** | A `compareTo` that returns 0 exactly when `equals` is true. (7.02) |
| **Constructor** | Code that initialises a new object; it has the class's name and no return type. (3.01) |
| **CRC-32** | A checksum used to detect accidental damage to data. (7.05) |
| **DataOutputStream** | Writes numbers and strings in a fixed big-endian binary format. (7.05) |
| **DateTimeFormatter** | Formats and parses dates and times with a pattern or a standard format. (7.04) |
| **Deadlock** | Threads waiting forever for locks the others hold. (6.04) |
| **Dynamic dispatch** | Choosing which overridden method to run from the object's actual class at run time. (3.03) |
| **Effectively final** | A local variable never reassigned, which lambdas may capture. (6.01) |
| **Encapsulation** | Keeping an object's data private and changing it only through its methods. (3.02) |
| **Endianness** | The order of a number's bytes: big-endian puts the high byte first, little-endian the low byte. (7.05) |
| **Enhanced for** | `for (T x : collection)`: a loop over every item. (1.05) |
| **Enum** | A type with a fixed set of named constants, which can have fields and methods. (3.05) |
| **equals / hashCode** | Value equality and its matching hash; overridden together. (3.03) |
| **equals contract** | The rules `equals` must follow: reflexive, symmetric, transitive, consistent, false for null. (7.02) |
| **Exception** | An object thrown to signal an error, caught with `try`/`catch`. (4.04) |
| **ExecutorService** | A pool of threads that runs submitted tasks. (6.04) |
| **Field** | A variable that belongs to an object (or to the class, if static). (3.01) |
| **final** | Cannot be reassigned (variables), overridden (methods) or extended (classes). (1.02) |
| **Functional interface** | An interface with exactly one abstract method, implementable by a lambda. (6.01) |
| **Garbage collector** | The JVM part that frees objects no longer referenced. (1.01) |
| **Generics** | Type parameters such as `List<String>`, checked at compile time. (4.01) |
| **Hash table** | An array of buckets indexed by hash code, giving O(1) average lookup. (5.04) |
| **hashCode contract** | Equal objects must return equal hash codes. (7.02) |
| **Immutable** | Cannot change after creation, like `String`, records and `LocalDate`. (3.02) |
| **Inheritance** | A class extending another and reusing its members. (3.03) |
| **Inner class** | A non-static nested class; each object holds a reference to an object of the outer class. (7.01) |
| **InputStream** | The abstract class for reading bytes; `read()` returns -1 at the end. (7.05) |
| **Instant** | A moment on the global timeline, the same everywhere. (7.04) |
| **Interface** | A contract of methods that implementing classes provide. (3.04) |
| **Invariant** | A condition that stays true, such as at the start of every loop round. (5.02) |
| **InvocationTargetException** | What `Method.invoke` throws when the called method throws; `getCause()` is the real exception. (7.03) |
| **Iterator** | An object that walks through a collection with `hasNext` and `next`. (5.03) |
| **JDK / JVM** | The Java Development Kit (compiler, tools, library) / the Java Virtual Machine that runs bytecode. (1.01) |
| **Lambda** | A short anonymous function: `x -> x * 2`. (6.01) |
| **Linked list** | Nodes that each hold a value and a reference to the next node. (5.03) |
| **Load factor** | Entries divided by buckets in a hash table; kept low by resizing. (5.04) |
| **Magic number** | Fixed bytes at the start of a file that identify its format. (7.05) |
| **Map** | Key-to-value lookup: `HashMap`, `TreeMap`, `LinkedHashMap`. (4.02) |
| **Memoization** | Storing results of earlier calls to avoid recomputing them. (2.04) |
| **Merge sort** | Divide-and-conquer sort: split, sort halves, merge; O(n log n), stable. (5.02) |
| **Method** | A named block of code with parameters and a return type. (2.01) |
| **Method reference** | Shorthand for a lambda calling one method: `String::length`. (6.01) |
| **NullPointerException** | Thrown when a member of `null` is used. (3.01) |
| **Object** | An instance of a class; also the root class of all classes. (3.01) |
| **Optional** | A container for a value that may be absent, used as a return type. (6.03) |
| **OutputStream** | The abstract class for writing bytes. (7.05) |
| **Overloading** | Several methods with the same name and different parameters. (2.01) |
| **Overriding** | A subclass replacing an inherited method. (3.03) |
| **Package** | A named group of classes matching a folder, such as `com.example.app`. (6.05) |
| **Pass by value** | Java copies argument values; for objects, it copies the reference. (2.01) |
| **Pattern matching** | Testing and taking apart values with `instanceof` and `switch` patterns. (3.05) |
| **Period** | An amount of calendar time in years, months and days. (7.04) |
| **Polymorphism** | Code written for a supertype working with any subtype's behaviour. (3.03) |
| **Primitive type** | One of the eight value types: `int`, `long`, `double`, `boolean`, `char`, `byte`, `short`, `float`. (1.02) |
| **Queue** | First in, first out: `offer` at the back, `poll` from the front. (4.02) |
| **Race condition** | A bug where the result depends on how threads' steps interleave. (6.04) |
| **Record** | A concise immutable data class with generated equals, hashCode and toString. (3.05) |
| **Recursion** | A method calling itself on a smaller problem. (2.04) |
| **Reference type** | A type whose variables hold references to objects. (1.02) |
| **Reflection** | Inspecting and using classes, fields, methods and constructors while the program runs. (7.03) |
| **Retention** | How long an annotation is kept: SOURCE, CLASS or RUNTIME (visible to reflection). (7.03) |
| **Scanner** | The class that reads text input, such as from `System.in`. (1.04) |
| **Sealed type** | An interface or class that lists the only classes allowed to implement or extend it. (3.05) |
| **Set** | A collection without duplicates: `HashSet`, `TreeSet`, `LinkedHashSet`. (4.02) |
| **Stable sort** | A sort that keeps equal items in their original order. (4.03) |
| **Stack** | Last in, first out: `push`, `pop`, `peek`. (5.04) |
| **static** | Belonging to the class rather than to an instance. (3.02) |
| **Static nested class** | A class declared inside another with `static`; it needs no object of the outer class. (7.01) |
| **Stream** | A pipeline of operations over a sequence of values. (6.02) |
| **StringBuilder** | A mutable buffer for building strings efficiently. (2.05) |
| **switch expression** | `switch` with `->` arms that produces a value. (1.05) |
| **synchronized** | Lets only one thread at a time run a block for the same lock. (6.04) |
| **Text block** | A multi-line string between `"""` delimiters. (1.04) |
| **Thread** | An independent path of execution. (6.04) |
| **try-with-resources** | `try (Resource r = ...)`, which closes the resource automatically. (4.04) |
| **Type erasure** | Generic types being removed after compile-time checking. (4.01) |
| **Unchecked exception** | A `RuntimeException`, which need not be declared or caught. (4.04) |
| **var** | Declares a local variable whose type the compiler infers. (6.03) |
| **Wildcard** | `?` in a generic type: `List<? extends Number>`. (4.01) |
| **Wrapper class** | The object version of a primitive: `Integer`, `Double`, `Boolean`... (2.03) |
| **ZonedDateTime** | A date and time in a particular time zone. (7.04) |
